title: Ryan Gravenberch Sent Off for Liverpool in Clash with Manchester City
seoTitle: Ryan Gravenberch Sent Off in Liverpool vs Man City
subtitle: The Liverpool midfielder receives a red card in a decisive Premier League match
excerpt: During the Anfield clash, Ryan Gravenberch receives two yellow cards and is sent off, leaving Liverpool down to ten men.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
In the Anfield clash between Liverpool and Manchester City, Ryan Gravenberch was sent off after receiving two yellow cards, leaving Liverpool down to ten men. The dismissal occurred in the second half following a tense challenge on Jeremy Doku.

How Gravenberch's sending-off changed the game

With Gravenberch off, Liverpool lost an important midfielder. Just three minutes later, Manchester City opened the scoring, extending their lead to 2–0. Being shorthanded contributed to Liverpool's defeat, which ended 3–0.

Pundits' reactions to the referee's decision

Jamie Carragher, on the Sky Sports panel, criticized the referee's decision, stating that Gravenberch's first challenge on Elliot Anderson did not warrant a card. Gary Neville, former Manchester United defender, agreed with Carragher, stating that the sending-off was correct.

Match context and Manchester City's situation

This was Manchester City's first match since the Premier League found them guilty of breaching financial rules involving disguised contracts with commercial partners. The club still maintains its innocence.

Details of the dismissal according to referee analysis

Referee Chris Kavanagh justified the sending-off by considering the second yellow card an "SPA" offense (stopping a promising attack). According to the analysis, Gravenberch may not have needed to make the challenge, but once he did, the referee was left with no other choice.

Impact on the scoreline and final result

  • First goal: Erling Haaland, 1–0
  • Second goal: Jeremy Doku, 2–0
  • Third goal: Rayan Cherki, 3–0

The final score was 3–0 to Manchester City, with Liverpool winning for only three minutes after Gravenberch's dismissal.

With information from The Sun, BBC.
